workflows.name: Create daily outreach leads and Gmail drafts from Google Maps with Apify and Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every weekday at 6 AM, scrapes Google Maps via Apify to find new businesses for rotating search-and-city pairs, logs them to Google Sheets, and creates Gmail drafts from your own template (never sent) using role-based inboxes discovered from each company’s website.

How it works
Runs on a schedule Monday to Friday at 6 AM (or can be started manually).
Finds an existing Google Sheet by name in Google Drive or creates it with a Leads tab and header row on the first run.
Reads existing leads from Google Sheets, rotates to today’s search and city, and uses Apify’s Google Maps Scraper to fetch up to 20 places.
Filters out closed listings, places without websites, and any company whose website domain already exists in the sheet, keeping up to the configured daily limit.
Uses Apify’s Website Contact Extractor to crawl each website and select a role-based inbox address (for example info@ or hello@) while ignoring personal-looking addresses.
For companies still missing an inbox, runs Apify’s Website Email Scraper and applies the same role-inbox selection rules to fill any remaining gaps.
Appends one row per new company to the Google Sheets Leads tab and creates a Gmail draft for each lead that has an inbox using the configured subject/body template.

Setup
Install the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify and add Apify credentials for the Apify nodes.
Add Google Sheets OAuth credentials (used for both Google Sheets and Google Drive/Sheets HTTP requests) so the workflow can find or create the spreadsheet and write to the Leads tab.
Add Gmail credentials and confirm you are comfortable with the workflow creating drafts only (it does not send emails).
Update the Settings values (sheet name, searches, cities, daily lead limit, sender name, and the email subject/body template placeholders) to match your outreach needs.

Requirements
An Apify account, the Google Sheets/Drive and Gmail credentials, and the community node @apify/n8n-nodes-apify. Cost in our tests was about $0.08 per daily run at Apify Store prices (10 new companies); the Maps search costs about $0.02 even on days with no new companies. Each Apify node has a maximum cost per run.

Customization
Edit the Settings node: one search per line, one city per line (one search × city pair per weekday), newPerDay, sender name, and the subject/body with {company}, {city}, {category} and {sender} placeholders. The role-inbox list (info, hello, events, sales, …) is in the inbox-picking Code node.

Additional info
How this differs from existing Google Maps outreach templates: most of them send the email for you (one email per lead, a CSV mailed to you, or an automated sequence). This one never sends: it only creates Gmail drafts you review. It writes only to role inboxes the company publishes on its own website, never to a person's address. It runs daily and incrementally (known domains are skipped, N new per day, rotating searches), needs no AI key, Airtable or CRM, and creates its own Sheet on the first run. Whether you may email a company depends on your country's rules; check before you send.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs daily to scrape WordPress.org plugin data and 1-star reviews using the Apify StoreIntel WordPress Plugin Directory Scraper, filters for valid B2B records, and saves the enriched results to Google Sheets.

How it works
Runs every day at 8:00 on a schedule.
Sets the Apify actor slug and the scraper input (plugin slugs/URLs, review scraping enabled, and a 1-star rating filter).
Calls the Apify API to run the StoreIntel WordPress Plugin Directory Scraper and return the dataset items.

Connect Google Sheets OAuth credentials and set the destination Google Sheet ID and sheet/tab name for the append-or-update action.

workflows.name: Turn Gmail lead replies into follow-up tasks with OpenAI and Google Sheets

user.name: Daniel Lubin
user.bio: I build websites and AI automations that make your business money while you sleep. Custom websites that rank on Google and turn visitors into calls, plus AI automations that capture, answer and follow up on every lead. Every template here is tested end to end and ships with plain-English setup notes. Based in Dallas, working with clients everywhere. Templates and done-for-you installs at daniellubin.com.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow monitors Gmail for new lead replies, uses OpenAI to classify intent and suggest next steps, logs each follow-up to Google Sheets, and emails you alerts, draft replies, and a daily due-today digest.

How it works
Triggers every minute for new Gmail inbox replies (excluding your own mail, promotions/social, and messages already labeled as logged) and also runs each morning on a schedule.
Cleans each new email by extracting sender/subject and the latest reply text, and skips newsletters, automated senders, and empty messages.
Sends the cleaned reply to OpenAI to classify the intent, summarize the message, propose a next step, and extract any follow-up date or referral contact.
Validates the OpenAI output, assigns a priority/status and a due date (or marks the item as “needs review” when confidence is low or parsing fails), then routes actions based on intent.
Emails you immediately for hot leads and “needs review” items, and for questions generates a reply draft and saves it to Gmail without sending.
Appends every processed reply as a new row in a Google Sheets “Follow-ups” tab and then applies a Gmail label to the original message so it is not processed twice.
Each morning, reads the Google Sheet for open or “needs review” follow-ups due today or overdue and emails you a prioritized list.

Setup
Connect Gmail credentials with permission to read messages, create drafts, send notification emails, and manage labels.
Add an OpenAI credential and select a compatible chat model in the OpenAI steps.
Connect Google Sheets credentials and create a spreadsheet with a tab named “Follow-ups” containing the required header columns used by the append step.
In Gmail, create a label that matches the configured label name (default: “Follow-up logged”).
Update the Settings values, including your Google Sheet URL, alert email address, name, business context, timezone, and any thresholds like min_confidence and not_now_days.

workflows.name: Collect social media leads from Instagram and Facebook with Apify and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs every 6 hours to read pending keyword topics from Google Sheets, scrape related Instagram hashtags and Facebook posts via Apify, extract basic lead details (profile, post link, email, phone), and save deduplicated results back to a Google Sheets Leads tab.

How it works
Runs every 6 hours on a schedule trigger.
Reads rows from the Google Sheets “Topics” sheet and keeps only entries that are not marked Done and contain Keywords.
Selects the next pending topic and sends its keywords to Apify’s Instagram Hashtag Scraper and Facebook Post Search Scraper.
Extracts lead fields from each returned post (topic, area, post/profile links, name, email/phone from the text, and timestamp) and filters out invalid Facebook results.
Merges the Instagram and Facebook lead lists into a single stream.
Appends or updates rows in the Google Sheets “Leads” sheet, deduplicating by “Post Link,” and then updates the corresponding topic row to Status = Done.

Setup
Create a Google Sheet with a “Topics” tab (including at least Topic, Area, Keywords, and Status columns) and a “Leads” tab with columns matching the workflow fields (for example: Topic, Area, Platform, Post Link, Profile ID, Profile Link, Name, Email, Contact, Post Text, Collected At).
Connect Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials in n8n and update the spreadsheet document ID and sheet names if you are not using the provided ones.
Add an Apify API token (HTTP credential) and ensure the Apify actors apifyinstagram-hashtag-scraper and themineworksfacebook-post-search-scraper are available to your account.
(Optional) Adjust the schedule interval, results limits, and keyword formatting (comma-separated) to match your lead volume and scraping needs.

workflows.name: Score and log website leads with OpenAI, Google Sheets, Gmail and Slack

user.name: Penna & Pixel
user.bio: AI automations in n8n: lead intake, invoice reading, Google Sheets. Fixed-price builds.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives website lead form submissions via webhook, validates and scores them with an OpenAI-compatible chat completion API, logs every lead to Google Sheets, drafts a reply in Gmail for non-spam leads, and alerts a Slack channel when a lead meets the hot-score threshold.

How it works
Receives a POST request from a website form via a webhook endpoint.
Normalizes the submitted fields and rejects obvious bots or invalid submissions (for example, bad email, empty message, honeypot filled, or too many links) with a 422 response.
Sends the lead details and your business rules to an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint to generate a score, category, urgency, summary, budget, and a reply draft.
Parses the AI response and, if the AI fails or returns invalid JSON, falls back to simple rule-based scoring and a default reply so the lead still gets processed.
Appends the enriched lead record (including score, tier, summary, and any AI error note) to a Google Sheets tab.
Creates a Gmail draft reply for non-spam leads and posts a Slack message for hot leads, then responds to the webhook with a thank-you message (or debug details if enabled).

Setup
Create an OpenAI-compatible API credential using HTTP Header Auth (header name Authorization, value Bearer ) and set the base URL/model in the Settings values.
Connect Google Sheets credentials and set the target spreadsheet ID and tab name in the Settings values, ensuring the sheet has headers matching the columns written (for example received_at, name, email, phone, company, source, category, urgency, budget, score, tier, summary, message, ai_note).
Connect Gmail OAuth credentials for creating email drafts.
Connect Slack credentials and set the target channel name in the Settings values.
Copy the webhook Production URL and configure your website form to send submissions as a POST request to that endpoint (including fields like name, email, phone, company, and message).

workflows.name: Approve lead reply emails in Slack with Gmail and Google Sheets

user.name: Solokit Studio
user.bio: Solokit Studio makes small, tested tools for solo operators and small teams who run AI agents and automations. Our n8n templates keep a person in the loop before anything goes out to a customer, and each one is free to inspect and change. Open source workflows and tools: https://github.com/SolokitStudio. Free sampler of our agent skills: https://solokit33.gumroad.com/l/agent-skills-sampler

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives new lead form submissions via webhook, generates a draft reply (template-based, with an optional OpenAI enhancement), posts the draft to Slack for human approval, then sends the approved reply via Gmail and logs the outcome to Google Sheets.

How it works
Receives a POST request on a webhook with lead details such as name, email, message, and optional company.
Validates the payload, detects the lead intent from keywords, and builds a draft reply and email subject from templates (optionally generating an improved draft using OpenAI if enabled).
Posts the lead details and draft reply to Slack via an Incoming Webhook with a Review button that opens an n8n approval form.
Waits up to the configured number of hours for a reviewer to approve and optionally edit the reply, or to reject it.
If approved, sends the final reply to the lead using Gmail with the prepared subject and approved/edited body.
Appends a row to Google Sheets recording the lead details and the final status (sent, sent_edited, rejected, or expired).

Setup
Create a Slack Incoming Webhook for your review channel and paste its URL into the workflow’s configuration values.
Connect Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials and set the target spreadsheet ID and sheet/tab name, ensuring the sheet has the expected header columns.
Connect Gmail OAuth2 credentials for the account that sends approved replies.
If self-hosting n8n, set the public WEBHOOK_URL so the Slack Review button opens the approval form correctly.
(Optional) To use AI drafting, add an OpenAI API key as an HTTP Header Auth credential, select it on the OpenAI request step, and enable that step.

user.bio: Automation consultant & n8n Ambassador helping teams streamline sales, marketing and operations with AI-powered n8n workflows. Founder of Khaisa Studio and creator of 90+ ready-made n8n templates. Use my link to book a consultation for custom automation work.

workflows.description:
A cleaning company usually hears about a new office build-out weeks after the contractor hired someone. City permit feeds publish tenant improvement filings the day they are issued, while the space is bare and the contract undecided. This workflow reads that feed every weekday morning, matches each build-out to a business on Google Maps, scores the lead, and reads the best ones out loud before your first crew meeting.

Last updated: November 2026.

Quick Overview
Decodo fetches the last seven days of renovation and alteration permits from the feed URL, cost floor and keywords set in Config. Filter Permits keeps the ones above the cost floor that mention commercial space, and Skip Seen Permits drops repeats. Apify Google Maps looks up each address and returns the business name, phone, website and category, and DeepSeek scores the lead 1 to 10 with the likely use, the timing, a first line to say and the contact path. Leads go to a Google Sheet, the best few become a 45 second brief voiced with ElevenLabs, and Telegram and Gmail deliver it.

How it works
Weekday 07:00 runs Monday to Friday at 07:00, and Config builds the permit URL with a seven day window.
Fetch Permits with Decodo posts it to the web data API, Parse Permits reads the JSON, and Split Permits makes one item per permit.
Filter Permits keeps permits at or above minReportedCost whose work description matches a keyword.
Skip Seen Permits drops ids from earlier runs, Any New Permits? routes the rest, and Tell Nothing New answers an empty morning.
Limit Permits caps the batch at maxLeads, and Apify Google Maps searches each address with three results under a $0.50 charge ceiling.
Build Lead keeps the permit fields plus the first Maps match, One Lead Per Permit keeps one row per permit id, and Score Lead sends it to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
Lead Parser returns lead_score, likely_use, why_now, outreach_line and contact_path. Lead Row shapes the row, Append Lead to Sheet writes it to a Leads tab, and Collect Leads gathers the run.
Write Morning Brief ranks by score and asks DeepSeek for 110 to 130 words. Narrate Brief voices it with ElevenLabs, Send Brief Audio posts the mp3, and Email Lead Table mails the table.

Setup
Add the Decodo key as a Header Auth credential with Authorization: Bearer .
Connect Apify on Apify Google Maps. apifyActor in Config defaults to compass~crawler-google-places.
Connect a DeepSeek credential (OpenAI compatible) on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Brief Model.
Connect ElevenLabs on Narrate Brief and pick the voice. voiceId and eleven_multilingual_v2 sit in Config.
Connect Telegram on Tell Nothing New and Send Brief Audio, and set telegramChatId.
Connect Google Sheets on Append Lead to Sheet, set sheetId, and make a Leads tab with columns runDate, permitId, permitNumber, issueDate, address, communityArea, reportedCost, workDescription, businessName, businessPhone, businessWebsite, businessCategory, mapsRating, mapsReviews, leadScore, likelyUse, whyNow, outreachLine, contactPath.
Connect Gmail on Email Lead Table and replace user@example.com with your address.
Check permitsUrl and city. The default is Chicago dataset ydr8-5enu, and any Socrata feed with these field names works.
Run one test with maxLeads at 1 or 2 to check the Maps match and sheet row first.

Quick Answers
Does it chase the same permit twice?
Skip Seen Permits remembers permit ids from earlier runs, so each job goes out once.

What happens on a day with no new permits?
Tell Nothing New sends one Telegram line with the date and cost floor; nothing reaches Apify.

How much Apify credit can one morning burn?
maxLeads caps the addresses, each search returns three results, and the run stops at a $0.50 charge.

What if no business shows up at that address?
Build Lead writes "No business found at this address", and the scoring prompt tells the model not to invent one: why_now says the lookup was empty and contact_path points at the site office or the general contractor on the permit. Check a listed phone before calling it a prospect.

Additional info
Built with n8n. Need an assessment on your business? Feel free to reach out at https://khmuhtadin.com/consultation/

workflows.name: Score inbound B2B leads with OpenAI, Gmail, and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives inbound web form leads via webhook, validates and scores them using the OpenAI Chat Completions API, creates a Gmail draft reply for high-fit leads, and logs both accepted and rejected submissions to Google Sheets.

How it works
Receives an inbound lead submission as JSON via a POST webhook.
Normalizes the payload, validates required fields (including email and minimum message length), and routes invalid submissions to a Google Sheets “Rejected” log.
Sends valid lead details and your ideal-customer criteria to the OpenAI Chat Completions API to generate a JSON score, a short reason, and a suggested reply draft.
Parses the model response and assigns a status, falling back to a needs_human status if the model call fails or returns invalid JSON.
Creates a Gmail draft addressed to the lead when the score meets your threshold so a human can review and send it manually.
Appends every scored lead (including low-fit and needs_human) to a Google Sheets “Leads” sheet with the score, reason, and status.

Setup
Configure the inbound form or source system to POST lead JSON to the workflow’s production webhook URL.
Add an HTTP Header Auth credential for the OpenAI-compatible API (Authorization: Bearer ) and update the request URL if you use a non-OpenAI provider.
Connect your Gmail account for draft creation.
Connect Google Sheets, set the spreadsheet URL/ID in both Sheets nodes, and create “Leads” and “Rejected” sheets with matching columns (for example: received_at, name, email, company, message, score, reason, status).

workflows.name: Save new LinkedIn job-based B2B sales leads to Google Sheets with Apify
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Discover potential B2B sales opportunities through LinkedIn hiring activity. This workflow runs daily, scrapes recent job postings using Apify, filters out previously collected jobs, saves new leads to Google Sheets, and sends a Slack notification.

How it works
Runs every day at 08:00 on a schedule.
Uses the Apify Scraper to collect up to 100 recent job postings matching your selected job titles and location.
Removes previously collected jobs and duplicate job IDs within the current execution.
Checks whether any new job leads remain. If no new leads are found, the workflow stops without sending a notification.
Appends each new job record to Google Sheets with company details, job information, posting metadata, and lead status.
After the spreadsheet update succeeds, sends one Slack message summarizing the newly discovered leads, including company names, job titles, locations, and job links.

Setup
Connect your Apify account in n8n and ensure you have access to the Rapid LinkedIn Scraper Actor.
Connect your Google Sheets OAuth2 credentials and select the spreadsheet and worksheet used to store job leads.
Connect your Slack account and configure the channel where new lead notifications should be delivered.
Configure the Apify input with your target job titles, location, maximum number of results, and posting date range.
Ensure your Google Sheets worksheet contains the required column headers, especially job_id, which is used to identify previously collected jobs.
Test the workflow to verify scraping, duplicate detection, spreadsheet updates, and Slack notifications before activating the daily schedule.

Requirements
An n8n instance with permission to install community nodes.
Apify account with access to the Rapid LinkedIn Scraper Actor.
Apify community node (@apify/n8n-nodes-apify) installed in n8n.
Google account with access to Google Sheets.
Slack workspace and permission to post messages in the selected channel.
A Google spreadsheet with the required job lead columns.

Customization
Job titles: Replace the default job titles with roles relevant to your target customers.
Location: Change the geographic location to focus on your preferred market.
Result limit: Adjust the maximum number of job postings collected per execution.
Posting date: Monitor jobs posted within the past 24 hours, past week, or past month.
Google Sheets: Customize the spreadsheet columns to match your prospecting process.
Slack notifications: Change the destination channel and customize the notification message.
Lead qualification: Extend the workflow with AI-powered company research, lead scoring, or CRM integrations.

Additional info
This workflow helps identify potential B2B sales opportunities by monitoring companies' hiring activity on LinkedIn. Hiring for specific roles can indicate business growth, new projects, or potential demand for relevant products and services.

Potential use cases:
SaaS companies discovering businesses that may need their products.
B2B sales teams identifying potential customers.
Marketing and lead generation agencies finding growing businesses.
Consultants monitoring companies hiring for relevant roles.
Business development teams tracking hiring activity in target markets.
The workflow stores newly discovered job postings in Google Sheets and sends a Slack notification after successfully saving new leads. Existing job IDs are checked to prevent previously collected jobs from being added again.

You can customize job titles, locations, result limits, posting date ranges, Google Sheets destinations, and Slack notifications according to your prospecting requirements.

Resources:

Rapid LinkedIn Scraper: https://apify.com/worldunboxer/rapid-linkedin-scraper

Apify n8n Integration Documentation: https://docs.apify.com/platform/integrations/n8n

n8n Documentation: https://docs.n8n.io/

workflows.name: Text back missed callers and create leads with The Engine and Slack

user.name: The Engine
user.bio: The Engine is the all-in-one AI platform that connects marketing and sales for service businesses: content, ads and campaigns, plus Jessica, an AI sales agent that calls, texts, follows up and books appointments.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow receives call-status webhooks from your phone system, detects missed calls, then uses The Engine to send an SMS text-back and create a lead record, and finally posts an alert to Slack.

How it works
Receives a POST webhook from your phone system with call status and caller details.
Normalizes the payload (for Twilio-style form fields or generic JSON) to extract the caller phone number, name, and missed-call status.
Continues only when the event represents a missed call and a valid phone number is present.
Sends an automated SMS text-back to the caller via The Engine Messages API.
Creates a new lead in The Engine (with source and notes indicating the missed call) using The Engine webhook endpoint.
Posts a missed-call notification to the configured Slack channel including the caller number and confirmation that the text-back and lead save succeeded.

Setup
Create a The Engine API key with the required scopes and add it to n8n as an HTTP Header Auth credential using the header name X-API-Key.
Update the Config values for your The Engine user ID, business name, and text-back message, and set the Slack channel name to post alerts to.
Add a Slack credential/connection with permission to post messages to the target channel.
Copy the workflow’s production webhook URL for /missed-call and configure your phone system (for example, a Twilio Status Callback) to POST call events to it.

Additional info
Never lose a caller you could not answer. Point any phone system's call-status webhook (Twilio, RingCentral, Aircall and others) at this n8n workflow. It detects missed calls, texts the caller back within seconds through The Engine, saves the caller as a lead in The Engine so nothing slips, and alerts your team in Slack. A simple missed-call text-back for dental offices, med spas, contractors and other service businesses. The Engine works with any CRM and offers a 7-day free trial with 300 credits, no card needed.

How to set it up
Start The Engine at https://theengine.dev. In the Sales Engine go to Settings > API keys and create a key with the messages and webhooks scopes.
In n8n create a Header Auth credential (Name X-API-Key, Value your key) and select it on every node ending in "(The Engine)".
Open the Config node and fill in engine_user_id (the number in your webhook URLs under Settings > Webhooks), business_name and text_back_message.
Twilio: Phone Numbers > your number > Voice > Call status changes > this workflow's production URL (/webhook/missed-call), POST. Other systems: send JSON with from and status (or missed: true).
Add your Slack credential and channel.

Limits: texts go from The Engine's messaging number (not your business line) to US/Canada mobile numbers, capped at 10 per minute and 300 per day per account. The saved lead is created paused, so Jessica only follows up when you start it in The Engine.

workflows.name: Verify phone numbers and save leads with iBlueText and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow collects a lead’s name, phone number, and optional email via an n8n form, verifies the phone using iBlueText (iMessage or SMS), then appends or updates the verified lead in Google Sheets and sends a welcome text via iBlueText.

How it works
Starts when a user submits the first n8n Form with their name, mobile number, and optional email.
Normalizes the submitted phone number into international format and prepares a configurable welcome message.
Calls the iBlueText Verify API to send a 6-digit verification code and, if sending fails, shows an error completion page.
Prompts the user for the code in a second form and checks it against iBlueText.
If the code is wrong, prompts once more and re-checks the code, then ends with a “wrong/expired code” completion page if verification still fails.
When verification succeeds, formats a verified lead payload, appends or updates the record in Google Sheets matching on phone number, and sends a personalized welcome SMS/iMessage via iBlueText.
Shows a final “verified” completion page to the user.

Setup
Create an iBlueText account, generate an API key, and add an n8n HTTP Header Auth credential using Authorization: Bearer  for the iBlueText requests.
Create a Google Sheets OAuth credential in n8n and select the target spreadsheet and sheet in the Google Sheets append/update step.
Ensure your Google Sheet has columns for name, phone, email, channel, and verified_at, and keep phone as the matching key to prevent duplicates.
Update the default country code logic (if needed) in the phone-normalization step and edit the welcome message text to match your brand.
Activate the workflow and share the n8n form URL for the initial phone number collection form.

Requirements
An iBlueText account (free to start, first 10 verifications free) and an API key. A Sandbox test key (sk-ibt-test-) lets you test without texting anyone; the code is always 000000.
A Google Sheets account and a sheet with the headers name, phone, email, channel, verified_at.
For the welcome text: a sending line on your iBlueText account (a free trial line works). Codes themselves go out from iBlueText's own numbers.

Customization
Change the welcome text in Your settings; {first_name} becomes the lead's first name. Keep it a question with no link for the best reply rate.
Set your default country code (DEFAULT_CC) in Clean phone number, e.g. '+44' or '+61'.
Swap Save lead to Google Sheets for your CRM (HubSpot, Airtable, Notion...) or add more fields to the first form page.
Edit the form titles and the verified, wrong-code and couldn't-send pages to match your brand.

workflows.name: Turn GEO Search Leads SEO audits into Jira or Trello task lists
workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow runs a GEO Search Leads full scan for a submitted website and turns the audit recommendations into prioritized implementation tasks in Jira or Trello, creating one parent item per scan and skipping tasks that already exist for the same site.

How it works
Receives a website URL, target language, client name, and a destination choice (Jira or Trello) from an n8n form.
Runs a GEO Search Leads full scan for the provided website.
Extracts findings from the scan, assigns priority and effort (S/M/L), generates task titles/descriptions with technical steps and “done when” criteria, and creates a stable GEO ID label per task to detect duplicates.
If Jira is selected, searches Jira for non-Done issues matching the generated GEO ID labels and removes any tasks that are already being tracked.
Creates a Jira Epic for the scan summary, then creates one Jira issue per new task, sets priority and labels, and links each issue to the Epic.
If Trello is selected, loads the Trello board for the target list, checks open cards for existing GEO IDs (ignoring archived/completed/Done-list cards), and removes any tasks that are already being tracked.
Creates a Trello “audit” parent card for the scan, then creates one Trello card per new task, adds a “Technical steps” checklist to each card, and adds a checklist on the audit card with links to the created task cards.

Setup
Create and connect a GEO Search Leads account here: https://app.geosearchleads.com/pages/register
For Jira output, add a Jira Software Cloud credential, then select the target Project and Issue Types for the Epic and task creation steps.
For Trello output, add a Trello API credential, then set the List ID used for creating both the audit card and task cards.
Optionally deactivate the Jira or Trello branch nodes if you only plan to use one destination, and adjust the form defaults (language/client name) to match your process.

workflows.name: Collect B2B leads with Dievio and Google Sheets
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Search for B2B contacts with Dievio through an authenticated webhook, save matching work-contact fields to a fixed Google Sheets tab, and return a row count. Each call retrieves one bounded page of results.

How it works
Receive a POST webhook request protected by a separate Header Auth credential, containing search filters and optional result settings.
Validate the request, require a configured spreadsheet destination, and return an HTTP 400 JSON response when the input is invalid.
Build one Dievio Search API request with a fixed endpoint, one result by default and a maximum of 100.
Normalize the returned records into the configured columns: names, job title, company, location, available work email and phone, LinkedIn URL and status fields.
Append matching rows to the fixed Google Sheets tab using RAW cell values, then return counts and the hasMore flag.
When there are no matching records, skip Google Sheets and return writtenRows: 0. No automatic pagination or deduplication is performed.

Setup
In Webhook In, configure a Header Auth credential with header name X-Webhook-Secret. Your calling client must send the private value you choose.
In Run Dievio Search, select a DIFFERENT Header Auth credential with header name X-API-Key and your own Dievio API key. API calls use your Dievio API credit balance.
In Prepare Request, replace REPLACE_WITH_SPREADSHEET_ID with your spreadsheet ID and set the tab name. Connect a Google Sheets credential in Append Rows To Google Sheets and add the column headers from the README.
Listen for a TEST webhook event. POST a JSON body with maxResults: 1 and filters, with Content-Type: application/json and your webhook secret. Use includeEmails: true and emailStatus: work if you require a stored work email.
Inspect the returned counts and the sheet. No matches should return writtenRows: 0 without a Sheets call. Once your test works, activate the workflow and switch your client to the production webhook URL.

Requirements
An n8n instance, a Dievio API key with API credits, and a Google account with edit access to the target Google Sheets document.

Customization
Change the supported Dievio search filters, maxResults from 1 to 100, includeEmails, includePhones and emailStatus. Configure the spreadsheet destination directly in Prepare Request.

Additional info
Setup and example request: https://dievio.com/integrations/n8n
Source and exact column headers: https://github.com/hundevmode/n8n-dievio-b2b-lead-collector-template

The template is free. Dievio API calls use API credits. Contact fields may be unavailable for some profiles; this workflow does not check email deliverability. Phone retrieval is opt-in. Repeating a webhook call can create duplicate sheet rows. If Google Sheets fails after a successful API search, inspect the n8n execution before retrying.

workflows.description:
Quick overview
This workflow captures website contact form submissions, uses Google Gemini to classify the lead and draft a reply, logs every message to Google Sheets, and emails an internal alert for non-spam inquiries.

How it works
Receives a new submission from an n8n Form trigger with the visitor’s name, email, phone, and message.
Applies your business context, category list, preferred tone, notification email, and summary language to the incoming submission.
Sends the message and rules to Google Gemini to classify it, set an urgency level, write a one-line summary, and draft a reply, then parses the result into structured fields.
Formats the submission plus the AI results into a row and appends it to a Google Sheets spreadsheet.
If the category is not Spam, sends an email alert to your notification address with the summary and suggested reply, using the visitor’s email as Reply-To.

Setup
Add Google Gemini API credentials for the Gemini chat model node.
Create a Google Sheet with headers Date, Name, Email, Phone, Message, Category, Urgency, Summary, Reply draft, then connect Google Sheets (service account) and select the document and sheet.
Configure SMTP credentials for the email-sending node and set a valid From address/domain.
Update the Business settings values (business name/description, categories, reply tone, owner language, notification email and sender email) to match your business.

Requirements
Google Gemini API key (the free tier works) or any other chat model
Google account with Google Sheets (a service account is recommended)
SMTP account to send the alerts (e.g. Resend, Gmail or Outlook)

Customization
Replace the n8n Form with a Webhook to use your own website form
Edit categories, reply tone and languages in Business settings
Swap Gemini for OpenAI, Anthropic or any other chat model

Additional info
Replies are drafted in the customer's language and the summary in yours. Nothing is ever sent to the customer automatically: you review the draft and reply from your inbox.

Quick overview
This workflow collects a website URL via an n8n form, checks the page for lead-capture signals, uses Groq to generate a short audit summary, then logs the request to Google Sheets and emails a scored HTML report to the visitor and an alert to you via Gmail.

How it works
Receives an audit request from an n8n form submission with the visitor’s name, email, business name, and website.
Normalizes the inputs (including adding https:// when missing) and fetches the website HTML via an HTTP request.
Runs rule-based checks on the page to detect lead-capture elements (WhatsApp, booking, tap-to-call, contact form, live chat, opening hours, response-time promise, and mobile readiness) and calculates a weighted score out of 100.
If the page is readable, sends the check results and a text excerpt to Groq to generate a JSON audit summary with strengths, top fixes, and a quick win, then composes a branded HTML report.
If the page cannot be read or is unreachable, builds a “could not audit” email and marks the request for manual review or unreachable status.
Appends the audit outcome to an Audits tab in Google Sheets and emails the visitor their report and you an owner alert via Gmail.

Setup
Create a Groq API key and connect it in the Groq chat model used to write the audit summary.
Connect a Gmail account for sending the visitor report and the owner alert.
Connect Google Sheets, set the target spreadsheet document ID, and ensure a sheet tab named Audits exists with the expected columns.
Open the configuration step and replace the placeholders for your agency name, owner alert email, and booking link (and optionally update the CTA text and minimum readable character threshold).
Activate the workflow and publish or embed the n8n form, then share the form URL on your website.

workflows.name: Find and approve Apollo B2B cold email leads with OpenAI and Gmail
workflows.description:
Quick overview
Pulls B2B leads from Apollo or Google Sheets, verifies and qualifies them with Hunter and rule checks, researches each company website, drafts a cold email with OpenAI, emails the draft to a reviewer for one-click approval before optionally sending via Gmail and logging outcomes in Google Sheets (and HubSpot).

How it works
Runs on a weekday schedule or manual start, and also handles unsubscribe link clicks via a GET webhook.
Reads the Pipeline and Suppression tabs in Google Sheets, then pulls new leads from Apollo (search + bulk enrichment) or from a Leads tab.
Normalizes and deduplicates leads against existing Pipeline entries and the Suppression list, optionally verifies email deliverability via the Hunter Email Verifier API, and records disqualified leads as Skipped in the Pipeline tab.
For each qualified lead, fetches the company homepage, uses an OpenAI-powered agent to research the site (optionally reading up to two more on-domain pages and selecting an offer from the Google Sheets Offers tab), and keeps only facts whose quotes are found in the scraped website text.
Uses OpenAI to draft a short plain-text cold email from the validated facts, then runs rule-based quality checks and rewrites the draft up to the configured limit or marks it as Needs review/Failed.
Saves each lead’s research and draft status to the Google Sheets Pipeline tab and optionally upserts the contact into HubSpot.
For drafts marked Awaiting approval, emails the reviewer via Gmail with Approve/Reject links, waits for a click (or timeout), then re-checks Suppression and—if sending is enabled—sends the final email via Gmail with a signed one-click unsubscribe link.
When the unsubscribe webhook is called with a valid signature, appends the email/domain to the Suppression tab in Google Sheets and responds with a confirmation message.

Setup
Create a Google Sheets document with Pipeline, Suppression, and Offers tabs (and a Leads tab if you use lead_source = "sheet"), and paste the sheet URL into the Settings.
Add credentials for Google Sheets, OpenAI, Gmail, Apollo (HTTP Header Auth using x-api-key), and Hunter (HTTP Query Auth using api_key), plus HubSpot (App Token) if hubspot_sync is enabled.
Update all YOUR_ values in the Settings (company/offer text, reviewer_email, lead_source and Apollo search filters, and link_secret for signing unsubscribe links).
If you use Apollo, confirm your search criteria and max_leads_per_run to control enrichment credit usage.
Keep send_enabled set to false for initial testing, then set it to true when you are ready to send approved emails from Gmail.
Copy the production unsubscribe webhook URL and ensure your workflow base URL is reachable so recipients can click the unsubscribe link successfully.
